frontier.hypothesis: Site 161 (emitted `addu a0,a0,s4` vs target `addu a0,s4,a0`, 1 point) closes iff a body uses the VALUE form (a `s32 *tail` pointer local for the 0x114/0x118/0x11C loads) AND raises pri(tail qty) above the Judge[]-element quantity's 5000.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc allocates quantities in descending pri = floor_log2(refs)*refs*10000/span (BB2_QTY_DEBUG block 43). Body AB has the right operand order but refs=6 span=26 -> 4615 < 5000, so the Judge element takes $a0 first and the whole tail renames. Needed: span <= 23, or refs >= 7 (5384) / 8 (9230), or Judge span >= 5 (drops it to 4000). The tail quantity is COMBINED (the sll producer + the pointer), so one extra genuine reference is worth +1 ref.
frontier.next_probe: Do NOT re-run declaration-order or statement-order variants (AB1/AB2/A1/C4 all killed - birth/death do not follow source position). Two live routes: (a) find a semantics-preserving spelling that gives the tail pointer a SEVENTH reference without adding an instruction - e.g. routing one of the three loads' address through the pointer twice, or expressing `temp_a0_2` so its consumer re-references the pointer rather than the loaded value; (b) widen the Judge[]-element quantity from span 4 to span 5 by putting one independent instruction between its `lh` and the `mult` that consumes it. Measure with `wsl bash tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s24/qty.sh <tag>` and read the block-43 QTYDBG lines; the model predicts the seat before the sandbox does.

frontier.hypothesis: The last delay-slot divergence (emitted 45-47, 2 points) closes iff $v0 is live at the entry of jump_insn 78's TARGET block; the source-level route to that liveness is NOT block merging (killed) but putting a real value in $v0 across the branch.
frontier.mechanism: fill_slots_from_thread's steal_delay_list_from_fallthrough on insn 78 is refused only by insn_sets_resource_p (trial, &opposite_needed); opposite_needed is the exact flow live-in of the beq's target block (oppregs = 0x20000380 = {a3,t0,t1,sp}, cleanly resolved by find_basic_block from barrier 85, not the -1 conservative fallback). Target's compile must have bit 0x4 set in that word.
frontier.next_probe: s24 killed the block-merge route (R1a byte-neutral) - the live-in word is a flow fact, not a CFG-shape fact, so the remaining attack is to make some value genuinely LIVE in $v0 across the range chain into block_15: e.g. hoisting the `D_800A3824` load (or the `*(s16 *)(arg0 + 4)` read that feeds temp_a1_2) above the range chain so its pseudo is live-in at code_label 87, and checking whether RA seats it in $v0. Instrument with `wsl bash tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s24/dbr.sh <tag>` and read the `thr insn=78 ... oppregs=` word; if bit 0x4 sets, the two points close. Do NOT re-run Q1/Q2-style relocations of the `return 1;` block (10 / 215 and 8 / 216) or R1a.

frontier.hypothesis: The MEM-address-vs-pointer-value expansion law (E-s24-2) is a general, reusable lever for this codebase, not a one-off for this function.
frontier.mechanism: Every commutative `addu` of a pointer and a scaled index in a GCC 2.7.2 -mel build has its operand order fixed at expand by whether the plus is expanded via memory_address (EXPAND_SUM -> shift first) or as a plain value (source order). A whole class of one-point `addu operand order` residuals elsewhere in the queue is therefore a one-line respelling, not a search.
frontier.next_probe: Cheap and out-of-band for this function: when any other grind ledger reports an `addu rd,rA,rB` vs `addu rd,rB,rA` residual on a pointer+index sum, check whether the C spells it as a pointer local or as an inline address and flip that, then verify with the .rtl dump. Worth a line in docs/grind/decisions.md or a technique rule if a second function confirms it.
